newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Luxembourg 1995 current account surplus 93 bln Luf.
newsitem.headline: Luxembourg 1995 current account surplus 93 bln Luf.

text.p: Luxembourg had a current account surplus of 92.8 billion Luxembourg francs in 1995, compared with 90.8 billion in 1994 and 79.1 billion in 1993, the country's statistics office said on Monday.

It is the first time since the Belgo-Luxembourg economic union (BLEU) was formed that Luxembourg has reported a balance of payments breakdown. It has to so so under the rules of the Maastricht Treaty on European economic and monetary union.
Most of the country's current account surplus was generated by services, of which by far the largest portion was due to financial services.
The current account is the measure of Luxembourg's financial position vis-a-vis the rest of the world, measuring both trade in goods, services and investments.
The Belgian National Bank said on Friday Belgium's current account surplus was 312 billion Belgian francs in 1995, or 76 percent of the total of the BLEU.
